s: Network Dissection quantifies interpretability by aligning individual units of vision networks with human-labelled concepts.

t: Axiomatic Attribution for Deep Networks
s: Proposes Integrated Gradients, an axiomatic attribution method for deep networks.

t: Towards A Rigorous Science of Interpretable Machine Learning
s: Proposes application-, human- and functionally-grounded evaluation as a rigorous science of interpretability.

t: Reluplex: An Efficient SMT Solver for Verifying Deep Neural Networks
s: Introduces Reluplex, an SMT-based method for formally verifying properties of ReLU neural networks.

t: The Off-Switch Game
s: Shows that an agent uncertain about its objective has an incentive to let humans switch it off, whereas a certain agent does not.

t: Logical Induction
s: Constructs a computable algorithm that assigns probabilities to logical statements and outpaces any efficient deductive process, satisfying many desirable properties of reasoning under logical uncertainty.

t: Stealing Machine Learning Models via Prediction APIs
s: Demonstrates that ML models offered through prediction APIs can be extracted (stolen) from their query outputs.

t: Concrete Problems in AI Safety
org: Google Brain / Stanford / UC Berkeley / OpenAI · Google Brain, OpenAI, Stanford, UC Berkeley · OpenAI / Google Brain / Stanford / UC Berkeley
s: Agenda paper naming five practical accident-risk problems: side effects, reward hacking, scalable oversight, safe exploration and distributional shift.

t: Cooperative Inverse Reinforcement Learning
s: Formalises value alignment as a cooperative game in which a robot learns a human's reward function by observing and assisting them.

t: Self-Modification of Policy and Utility Function in Rational Agents
s: Analyses when rational agents have incentives to modify their own policy or utility function.

t: Practical Black-Box Attacks against Machine Learning
s: Shows black-box models can be attacked by training a local substitute model and transferring adversarial examples.

t: Alignment for Advanced Machine Learning Systems
s: Research agenda on alignment problems specific to ML systems, such as inductive ambiguity, robust objectives and mild optimization.

t: Quantilizers: A Safer Alternative to Maximizers for Limited Optimization
v: AAAI Workshop on AI, Ethics, and Society / MIRI
s: Proposes quantilizers, which sample from the top fraction of a base distribution instead of maximizing, limiting Goodhart-style failures.

t: Distillation as a Defense to Adversarial Perturbations Against Deep Neural Networks
s: Proposes defensive distillation as a defence against adversarial perturbations (later broken by stronger attacks).

t: Model Inversion Attacks that Exploit Confidence Information and Basic Countermeasures
s: Shows that model confidence scores can be exploited to reconstruct sensitive training inputs such as faces.

t: Explaining and Harnessing Adversarial Examples
s: Explains adversarial examples by the linearity of neural networks and introduces the fast gradient sign method and adversarial training.

t: Intriguing properties of neural networks
s: Discovers adversarial examples: imperceptible perturbations that cause deep networks to misclassify inputs.

t: Evasion Attacks against Machine Learning at Test Time
s: Formalises test-time evasion of machine-learning classifiers as an optimisation problem solved with gradients.

t: Poisoning Attacks against Support Vector Machines
s: Introduces gradient-based poisoning attacks that inject crafted training points to degrade support vector machines.
